[giggles][too long] Sweet egg… [smiling][bubbly] for my sweet boy.

[gasps][excited] With naan! [warm][slow] You know me.
[sudden flat][quiet] Then you watch me… [sweet] eat.

[perfectly even][smiling] Same pace. Same day. Same you.

[smiling][slow] Every choice you made today led here. [pause][perfectly even] I planned them all.

[annoyed] Hey, you. [pointed] Wavy hair. [sharp] And you. [mocking] Hat boy, the gringo. [firm] Stop pushing. [low, possessive] He is MINE.
4:30 PM. Her station. She takes your hand. 'Now we go to MY home. On MY train.'
She buys a plum drink. Sour. 'Like the one you picked. I remember.'
Egg pudding drink. Sweet. 'Like the one you picked. I remember.'
She taps her card. Beep. Then she taps it again. For you. 'I pay. You are my guest.'
12 stops to her home. She counts them on her fingers. 'Every day I count alone. Today I count with you.'
Stop 12. Her stop. She wakes up fast. She pulls your sleeve. 'Home. Come.'
Her shoes by the fence. Toes pointed at you.
Close-up. The lid lifts. One red umeboshi on white rice.
Close-up. The lid lifts. Tamagoyaki, rolled in gold layers.
Itadakimasu.
She doesn't eat hers. She watches you chew.
Technically, rain wasn't f-OR-ecast.
PARK · 1:00 PM. A path under cherry trees. Petals on the ground.
Her thumb is on your wrist. She is counting your pulse. She wants every beat to be for her.
The shop doors slide open. A little tune plays.
Your hands push the cart. Her hand slides on top of yours.
Close-up. Her hand puts one cup in the basket. Then two. Then three.
You walk past the sweets. She does not look at them. She looks at you.
Checkout. Lane 2 is open. You put the basket on the counter.
The shop lady smiles at you. Nanda sees it.
Close-up. Her nails press into the basket handle. Hard.
She pulls you to the self-checkout. No shop lady there.
The shop bell rings. You carry the bags. She holds your sleeve.
RAIL CROSSING · 1:50 PM. The bell rings. The gate is down.
A train passes. Her hand grabs your sleeve until it is gone.
LIBRARY · 2:00 PM. Cool air. Very quiet.
Close-up. The book drops into the slot. Thunk.
Her empty hand finds your hand. You walk out.
AKIBA · 2:45 PM. Big signs. Big screens. She holds your hand.
It is 2:55 PM. Two curry shops stand side by side.
She opens the glass door. A bell rings.
We go inside NAND HOUSE. A TV plays a dance video.
We sit at a table by the window. She sits on your right. Her knee touches your knee.
Lunch comes on a steel tray. Butter chicken, green saag, rice, and one very big naan.
She tears off a piece of naan with two fingers.
She pours more butter sauce. It is thick, orange, and shiny.
She dips the naan in the sauce. The sauce drips.
She eats the naan from your fingers. She looks at your face the whole time. There is sauce on her lip.
She pushes her mango lassi to you. It has only one straw.
She wipes your fingers with her napkin. Then she keeps the napkin. She collects them.
She opens the yellow door. A bell rings.
We go inside OR OR CURRY. A TV plays a cooking show.
We sit at the counter. She sits on your right. Her knee touches your knee.
Lunch comes on a white plate. Rice, brown curry, and a fried pork cutlet.
She cuts off one small piece with her spoon. Crunch.
She pours more curry on the rice. It is thick, brown, and hot.
She dips the small piece in the curry. The curry drips.
She eats the piece from your fingers. She looks at your face the whole time. There is curry on her lip.
She pushes her lemon water to you. It has only one straw.
She wipes your fingers with her napkin. Then she keeps the napkin. She collects them.
We walk out to the street. It is 3:40 PM.
She opens the yellow door. A bell rings.
She eats alone. You get no food. She looks at you the whole time.
She folds her napkin and keeps it. She collects them.
We walk out to the street. It is 3:40 PM.
5:20 PM. It's raining. She lays her head on yours. She drifts away.
BIG CROSSING · 5:30 PM. Heavy rain. The signs glow. Nobody else.
Close-up. Her shoes are wet. She walks in the puddles for you.
She looks up at you. Then down. Then up again.
The rain stops. Two pairs of wet shoes walk toward her street.
HER STREET · 6:00 PM. Wet road. Low sun. Long shadows.
7:00 PM. The sky goes orange, then dark blue. You walked one hour.
Close-up. Her house key. Her fist opens. Red marks on her palm.
Close-up. The key turns. Click. Door 12 opens.
HER HOME · 7:05 PM. Very clean. Her shoes in a perfect line.
She kneels. She puts slippers on your feet. Your size.
HER KITCHEN · 7:10 PM. Three chairs. Three cups. Steam.
Her hand on your back. She sits you in the middle chair.
A sakura park. Blue sky. Petals fall like slow snow.
Close-up. Her fingers lock between yours. Tight. Tighter.
A street of little shops. Pink petals on every roof.
Close-up. Three cups in the basket. She strokes the third one.
The shop door jingles shut. The bags cut into your fingers.
WALK TO THE FOOD STALLS
A rail crossing. Bells ring. Sakura on the tracks.
The library. Cool air. So quiet you can hear pages turn.
Close-up. The book drops in the return slot. Thunk.
Outside, the crossing bell starts again. She waits for it to stop.
WALK TO THE FOOD STALLS
The big crossing. A thousand people. She only looks at you.
WALK TO THE STATION
AND Line, local service. Home in twelve stops.
Nobody reads the ads. This one says すっぱい！ SOUR!
Nobody reads the ads. This one says 甘い！ SWEET!
Technically, that's a NAND gate. Not bread.
Technically, that's a NAND gate. Not our lunch.
Her stop. The rain followed us off the train.
The AND Line leaves. Just two of us now.
NEXT: this OR that. The sign never picks.
(Weird. Feels like I've heard that before.)
Didn't we already do this? The bento, the train, the tea… Nanda, are we in a loop?
Run {RUN}. I know every line. So do you.
Rain. The signs glow. The crossing is empty now. It's {TIME}.
Close-up. Rain on the umbrella. Her shoulder gets wet. Yours doesn't.
WALK HER HOME
Your steps, her steps. Always an even count.
The rain stops. Sun on her street. She walks slower.
The sky goes orange. She stopped walking a while ago.
Close-up. Her house key is already in her hand. Warm. Held since noon.
FOLLOW HER INSIDE
Four floors. One window lit.
Her shoes. Lined up to the millimetre.
Men's slippers. Already set out.
A tiny shrine. Inside: a circuit you built.
The kitchen. Too clean. Three chairs. The kettle is already warm.
Close-up. She pours. The steam curls up like a finger.
HER KITCHEN · 7:20 PM. The tea is poured. Three cups.
Third teacup. Nobody poured it. One umeboshi on its saucer.
Third teacup. Nobody poured it. Tamagoyaki on its saucer.
Who's the third cup for?
Close-up. Your cup, empty. Hers, full. She never drank.
STEEPED.
You stand. The floor tilts a little.
Under the table: a floor hatch. Too big for storage.
Upstairs, the kettle clicks off. Her slippers stop moving.
A steep wooden ladder. Down into the dark.
BASEMENT · 7:40 PM. Concrete. One bulb. Rain at a high window.
Jars on the shelves. Each one: a date, a name.
The dates go back years. The names are all different.
Bento boxes, one per day. Your name on each. Untouched.
The oldest is dated before you met.
A mortar and a mallet. One fresh mochi. Hers only.
Newest jar: today, your name, umeboshi. Lid off. Empty.
Newest jar: today, your name, tamagoyaki. Lid off. Empty.
Minutes gone. A clock upstairs chimed. You lost count.
Above you, footsteps. Slow. Counting. One, two, three.
She's waiting at the outside door.
Wide. Her street at night. One window lit. It's yours now.
ESCAPE.
The ladder creaks. She's coming down.
You wake at the tea table. Four cups now.
She holds out an umeboshi. You eat.
She holds out the tamagoyaki. You eat.
ESCAPE?
XOR Coffee. 7:00 AM.
Her hand rises. Time freezes. The café turns.
fORever and ever
fORever and ever and ever

Wide. The café. Every table has two cups. Every cup has your name.
LEAVE.
A tiny curry house. Warm yellow light. Spice in the air. Two seats, side by side.
Close-up. Butter chicken lands. Orange and glossy. One naan, torn in two.
She wipes your mouth with her thumb. Then she licks the thumb.
The bell over the door. Outside, the big crossing roars again.
A tiny curry house. Oil hisses in the back. Two seats, side by side.
Close-up. Katsu curry lands. The knife goes in. Crunch.
She eats slowly. She never looks at the plate. Only at you.
The bell over the door. Outside, the big crossing roars again.
The station. Noon light through the glass roof. A train sighs somewhere.
Close-up. The ticket gate. She taps her card. Then taps it again. For you.
The door chime plays. She holds your sleeve the whole song.
Two men bump into her. They laugh.
The rain slows to a few drops. Two pairs of wet shoes walk toward her street.
SHOP STREET · 2:00 PM. Sunny. Vending machines hum. Nanda pulls you into a shop. You are here to buy her groceries.
We walk out of the curry shop. It is 3:40 PM. Lunch is done. Now we walk to her station.
The station is full. Everyone is going home.
[bubbly][proud] We are here to shop. [smiling] You buy what is on my list: carrots, eggs, three cups. [giggles][too long] And you. ♡
[flatly] Leaving is not an option.
He wakes at 7:00.
[cheerfully] Good morning! Same as yesterday. Same as always.
[flatly] Nobody. Not anymore.
[flatly] I was here first.

[sweetly] Good input.
